title: Cross-Document Event-Keyed Summarization
authors: William Walden; Pavlo Kuchmiichuk; Alexander Martin; Chihsheng Jin; Angela Cao; Claire Sun; Curisia Allen; Aaron Steven White
task_description: Generate a summary for a target event by synthesizing accounts from multiple source documents; includes cross-document argument extraction and source/report ablations.
inputs: Report and source articles; target event/frame representation; cross-document evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Expert-annotated single- and cross-document summaries; event arguments; human evaluation and baseline scores.
pipeline_gap_filled: cross-source evidence aggregation; provenance-aware argument extraction; inspectable intermediate event arguments
artifact_access_status: Public official repository; data/seamus.zip and model outputs are identified in README.
license_status: CC-BY-SA-4.0 stated by repository; verify data component terms separately.
evidence_basis: ACL page and PDF state SEAMuS is a dataset/benchmark for CDEKS synthesizing the same event across multiple sources and based on expert reannotation of FAMuS. Official repository states downloadable data/seamus.zip.
limitations: Same-event news/source reporting rather than unrelated scholarly authors; output is event summary rather than a new argumentative thesis.
why_relevant: Closest located benchmark for explicit cross-document synthesis with exposed argument structure and source/report provenance.

title: FAMuS: Frames Across Multiple Sources
authors: Siddharth Vashishtha; Alexander Martin; William Gantt; Benjamin Van Durme; Aaron Steven White
task_description: Validate whether a candidate source describes a report event and extract cross-sentence event arguments from report plus source.
inputs: Wikipedia report passages; genre-diverse source articles; event trigger and candidate sources.
outputs_or_labels: FrameNet event/frame and cross-sentence argument annotations; source-validation labels; report/source argument tables.
pipeline_gap_filled: source provenance; cross-document claim/argument alignment; dependency-preserving evidence selection
artifact_access_status: Paper provides dataset description and task definitions; artifact URL is the scholarly preprint, but a stable data download was not confirmed.
license_status: Not confirmed from opened sources; do not infer from paper access.
evidence_basis: ACL page/PDF state over 1,255 reports, 253 event types, five supporting documents per type, and two cross-document tasks.
limitations: Extraction/alignment is not free-form novel argument construction; source pairs are event-linked and mostly news/Wikipedia.
why_relevant: Provides reusable intermediate cross-source argument labels that can scaffold a stronger synthesis benchmark.

title: M3SciQA: A Multi-Modal Multi-Document Scientific QA Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models
authors: Chuhan Li; Ziyao Shangguan; Yilun Zhao; Deyuan Li; Yixin Liu; Arman Cohan
task_description: Answer expert questions requiring cross-referencing an anchor paper with cited papers and interpreting text, figures, and tables.
inputs: 1,452 expert questions; 70 NLP paper clusters; anchor paper plus cited documents; multimodal evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Answers and question annotations; paper-cluster/document evidence; model and human evaluation results.
pipeline_gap_filled: cross-source scholarly evidence retrieval and integration; provenance over cited literature
artifact_access_status: ACL PDF identifies 1,452 questions across 70 clusters and links the official GitHub repository.
license_status: Dataset license/access terms not verified in opened evidence.
evidence_basis: ACL page/PDF explicitly frames the benchmark as multi-document scientific reasoning over anchor papers and cited documents.
limitations: QA answer targets are generally not novel arguments; cross-document dependence may be comparative or lookup-like.
why_relevant: Strong scholarly-domain control for testing whether a system combines evidence from unrelated papers before synthesis.

title: Towards Multi-Document Question Answering in Scientific Literature: Pipeline, Dataset, and Evaluation
authors: Hui Huang; Julien Velcin; Yacine Kessaci
task_description: Answer questions generated from citation-network communities with an automated filter enforcing dependence on multiple papers.
inputs: Thematically coherent academic-paper communities; citation-linked papers; multi-document questions.
outputs_or_labels: 6,804 QA pairs; document-dependence filtering; retrieval and QA evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: cross-source scholarly synthesis and retrieval; explicit inter-paper dependency
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF states 6,804 QA pairs, citation-network communities, multi-document dependence filtering, and released code/data; official GitHub README states dataset and Apache-2.0 code repository.
license_status: Questions/answers are automatically generated and QA-shaped; not necessarily argumentative or open-ended thesis construction.
evidence_basis: Most direct located benchmark for enforcing that complete answers require multiple scholarly documents.

title: ResearchBench: Benchmarking LLMs in Scientific Discovery via Inspiration-Based Task Decomposition
authors: Yujie Liu; Zonglin Yang; Tong Xie; Jinjie Ni; Ben Gao; Yuqiang Li; Shixiang Tang; Wanli Ouyang; Erik Cambria; Dongzhan Zhou
task_description: Retrieve inspiring papers, compose a research hypothesis from a research question and inspirations, and rank hypotheses.
inputs: 2024 scientific papers across 12 disciplines; research questions; gold inspiration papers; candidate hypotheses.
outputs_or_labels: Retrieval, hypothesis-composition, and pairwise ranking tasks; 1,369 paper records and task splits in official release.
pipeline_gap_filled: novel argument/hypothesis construction from multiple scholarly sources; inspiration provenance
artifact_access_status: ArXiv abstract states inspiration retrieval, hypothesis composition, and ranking over 2024 papers; official repository documents task files and counts.
license_status: Hypothesis composition may not require explicit claim-premise-warrant/proof skeleton; published status/version should be tracked because arXiv and ACL dates differ.
evidence_basis: Closest benchmark to constructing a genuinely new claim from source literature, though argument provenance and proof-level attribution remain under-specified.

title: DiscoveryBench: Towards Data-Driven Discovery with Large Language Models
task_description: Solve data-driven discovery tasks derived from published research workflows and natural-language discovery goals.
inputs: Datasets with metadata; discovery goals; task workflows derived from published papers across six domains.
outputs_or_labels: 264 discovery tasks and success metrics against known discovery goals.
pipeline_gap_filled: research-workflow synthesis and novel inference; structured discovery evaluation
artifact_access_status: ArXiv abstract states 264 tasks across six domains, with each task defined by a dataset, metadata, and discovery goal.
license_status: Not specifically multi-document input or source-attributed argument composition; artifact URL/license not confirmed from opened page.
evidence_basis: Useful control for whether synthesis produces a defensible discovery result rather than only fluent text.

title: MultiHop-RAG: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-Hop Queries
task_description: Retrieve and combine supporting evidence across multiple hops/documents to answer multi-hop queries.
inputs: Knowledge base/documents; multi-hop questions; supporting evidence.
outputs_or_labels: Answers plus supporting evidence and retrieval metrics.
pipeline_gap_filled: disputation retrieval; evidence aggregation; provenance-preserving selection
artifact_access_status: Search result and paper identity identify a benchmark with knowledge base, multi-hop queries, answers, and supporting evidence; artifact URL is the official-looking project repository.
license_status: Primarily QA and answer support, not generation of a new argument or explicit premise/warrant graph.
evidence_basis: Good retrieval/evidence-aggregation control to pair with a novel-argument synthesis task.

title: RoMQA: A Benchmark for Robust, Multi-evidence, Multi-answer Question Answering
authors: Victor Zhong; Weijia Shi; Wen-tau Yih; Luke Zettlemoyer
task_description: Answer clusters of questions derived from related constraints while handling multiple evidence and multiple valid answers.
inputs: Question clusters; Wikidata-derived constraints; evidence passages/entities.
outputs_or_labels: Multiple answers and evidence-grounded evaluation; robustness tests.
artifact_access_status: ACL record identifies RoMQA as the first robust multi-evidence, multi-answer QA benchmark and describes Wikidata-derived question clusters.
license_status: Knowledge-graph constraints and QA format do not require novel synthesis or scholarly documents; artifact/license not verified.
evidence_basis: Control for evidence completeness and non-single-answer evaluation when scoring open synthesis.

title: WikiHowQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multi-Document Non-Factoid Question Answering
authors: Valeriia Bolotova-Baranova; Vladislav Blinov; Sofya Filippova; Falk Scholer; Mark Sanderson
task_description: Generate grounded passage-level answers to how-to questions requiring reasoning over multiple documents.
inputs: How-to questions; 74,527 supporting documents; retrieved relevant passages.
outputs_or_labels: 11,746 human-written answers; highlighted supporting passages; human groundedness/factual-consistency evaluation.
pipeline_gap_filled: cross-document evidence aggregation; inspectable support selection; open-ended output evaluation
artifact_access_status: ACL page/PDF states 11,746 answers, 74,527 supporting documents, highlighted support, and public code/data.
license_status: Web how-to answers are not scholarly premises and usually answer practical questions rather than build a novel claim.
evidence_basis: Useful evaluation design for grounded open-ended synthesis and human inspection of support coverage.

title: Do Multi-Document Summarization Models Synthesize?
task_description: Test whether multi-document summarizers synthesize novel combinations or merely copy/extract information.
inputs: Document sets and generated summaries; source-document content and reference summaries.
outputs_or_labels: Synthesis-focused diagnostic analyses/metrics and model comparisons.
pipeline_gap_filled: novel synthesis diagnostic; separation of extraction from composition
artifact_access_status: ArXiv/TACL record explicitly asks to what extent MDS models perform synthesis and evaluates that question.
license_status: Evaluation study rather than a reusable benchmark artifact; summary synthesis is not argument/provenance structured.
evidence_basis: Direct conceptual and diagnostic precedent for distinguishing extractive aggregation from genuinely new cross-source content.

title: Multi-hop Evidence Retrieval for Cross-document Relation Extraction
task_description: Retrieve evidence across documents to infer relations that are not stated in any single document.
inputs: Entity pairs; document collections; cross-document relation instances.
outputs_or_labels: Relations with multi-hop evidence paths and retrieval/evidence evaluation.
artifact_access_status: Search result for the paper states cross-document relations require open-space evidence retrieval and inference across documents.
license_status: Relation extraction is narrower than natural-language argument synthesis; artifact access not verified.
evidence_basis: Relevant structural primitive: the desired argument can be scored by whether each premise path is sourced and necessary.
